workflow: A caller constructs an executable object with deliberately malformed encoded location metadata.
A diagnostic or inspection operation decodes the metadata assuming its encoding invariants are valid.
The malformed continuation pattern violates the decoder’s expected byte structure.
An internal assertion fires during decoding, terminating the process instead of reporting invalid metadata as a recoverable error.
summary: Malformed encoded metadata triggers fatal decoder assertion
decision_reason: The failure is caused by malformed variable-length metadata provoking an internal decoder assertion. Existing clusters involving truncated metadata over-reads or inconsistent object field counts have materially different failure mechanisms.
